body: Heavy rainfall and rising humidity put real stress on door frames, lock hardware, and deadbolts across Alachua, FL every storm season. What starts as a dragging door or a stiff deadbolt can turn into a lock you cannot throw at all. This post covers the main causes of storm-related door problems, the fixes you can handle yourself, and the situations where a locksmith gets things working again fast.
Why Does Storm Season Cause Swelling Doors in Alachua?

Wood absorbs moisture, and Florida's humidity regularly exceeds 80 percent during storm season. Extended wet periods give wood doors and frames very little time to dry out. When the door expands, it presses against the frame and the deadbolt no longer lines up with the strike plate. Older Alachua homes built before 2000 often have at least one exterior door with wood components that expand in wet conditions. Swelling is usually temporary, but the hardware problems it creates can persist even after the door dries out if the strike plate or bolt alignment has shifted.
What Causes a Deadbolt to Stick or Refuse to Turn After a Storm?
A sticking deadbolt after a storm is almost always caused by one of three things:

• The door has swollen and is pressing the bolt housing out of alignment
  • The strike plate opening has shifted relative to the bolt throw
  • Debris and moisture have worked their way into the lock cylinder

If the deadbolt feels stiff and grinds when you turn the key, moisture inside the cylinder is likely the issue. If the bolt moves freely but catches on the strike plate edge, alignment is the problem. If the door has to be pushed or pulled hard to seat the bolt, the frame has moved and the hardware needs adjustment. Quick Fixes You Can Try at Home

Some storm-season door problems respond well to basic maintenance you can do without calling anyone. Start with the lock cylinder. A dry graphite lubricant applied to the keyway can clear moisture buildup and restore smooth operation. Do not use WD-40 inside a lock cylinder since it leaves a residue that causes problems over time. If the door is visibly swollen, give it a few dry days once humidity drops. For a strike plate that is catching the bolt by a small margin, use a small file to widen the opening slightly so the bolt seats cleanly.

• Apply dry graphite lubricant to the keyway, not oil-based products
  • Check that door hinges are tight and have not loosened from repeated pressure
  • Inspect the weatherstripping for compression that may be binding the door
  • File the strike plate opening if the bolt is catching by a small amount
When Should You Call a Locksmith for Storm Door Problems?

Call a locksmith when the deadbolt will not extend fully and you cannot secure your home. A door that cannot lock is a security issue that should not wait. The same applies if the lock cylinder has been damaged by moisture and the key no longer turns smoothly after lubricant has been applied. Forcing a damaged cylinder can break the key off inside, which creates a more involved repair. Strike plate and frame alignment issues that go beyond what a small file can correct also need professional attention. Should You Upgrade Your Hardware Before the Next Storm Season?

If your locks have been sticking or your door frame has shifted multiple times, the hardware itself may be contributing to the problem. Older deadbolts with worn bolt mechanisms do not throw as cleanly as newer hardware, and worn strike plates give the bolt less room to seat. Replacing aged deadbolts and reinforcing strike plates with longer screws that reach the stud behind the frame reduces both storm-season problems and overall vulnerability. A new lock installation before storm season hits is a practical way to eliminate hardware that is already marginal. Smart lock options are worth considering if your door sees heavy use, and we handle smart lock installation for homeowners who want keypad or app-based access.
Protecting Your Locks and Doors Before the Next Storm

Applying a wood sealant or exterior paint to exposed wood door edges slows moisture absorption significantly. Replacing weatherstripping that has hardened or cracked reduces humidity reaching the door frame interior. Tightening hinge screws before storm season keeps the door hung at the correct angle, which directly affects deadbolt alignment. If your home has experienced repeated swelling in the same door, replacing it with a fiberglass or steel model eliminates the root cause.
